Article Title: Three golds in a day! Ankush Panghal completes Indian boxing hat-trick at Asian Games
Article Text:
Ankush Panghal

Ankush dominates the final

Lovlina and Parveen end 12-year wait

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Ankush Panghal completed a golden hat-trick for Indian boxing at the Asian Games on Friday, defeating South Korea’s Minseong Kim in the men’s 80kg final to cap a memorable day for the country’s pugilists in Aichi-Nagoya.Ankush dominated the title bout, winning the opening round 4-1 before taking the second unanimously 5-0 to establish a commanding advantage. He maintained his control in the third round, winning it 4-1 to seal the gold medal with a 4-0 verdict.His triumph came after Lovlina Borgohain and Parveen Hooda had won their respective finals, making Friday a landmark occasion for Indian boxing.Lovlina defeated China’s Ziyi Bao 5-0 in the women’s 75kg final on her 29th birthday, while Parveen edged Paris Olympics bronze medallist Chen Nien-chin of Chinese Taipei 3-2 in a split decision in the women’s 65kg category.The three victories gave India a hat-trick of boxing gold medals and brought a memorable end to a day of high-stakes contests.Ankush made an emphatic start against Kim, edging the opening round 4-1 on the judges’ scorecards. The Indian then raised his game in the second, securing a unanimous 5-0 verdict to move firmly in control of the contest.With the gold within reach, Ankush stayed composed in the final round and continued to outscore his Korean opponent.He won the round 4-1 to complete a commanding performance and claim the men’s 80kg title.The victory added another gold to India’s boxing haul after the women’s finals had already delivered two major milestones.Earlier, Lovlina produced a composed performance to defeat Bao and upgrade the silver she had won at the previous Asian Games. Her victory ended India’s 12-year wait for a women’s Asian Games boxing gold and made her only the second Indian woman after legendary MC Mary Kom to win the title.Mary Kom had claimed the women’s 51kg gold at the 2014 Asian Games in Incheon.“It was a very special birthday, I'm feeling really good. I thought I'd have to gift a gold medal on my birthday. It's the first time that I got a present for myself,” Lovlina said after her victory.Parveen followed with a hard-fought win over Chen, the Paris Olympics bronze medallist, to secure her maiden Asian Games gold. Her narrow split-decision victory added another landmark moment to India’s campaign.India’s boxing contingent had already surpassed its four-medal return from the previous edition, with Priya Ghanghas, Kapil Pokhariya and Narender Berwal also securing bronze medals.The country’s best Asian Games boxing performance remains the 2010 Guangzhou edition, where Indian boxers won nine medals, including two golds. Friday’s three-title sweep provided another memorable chapter in India’s campaign at Aichi-Nagoya.
Article Summary: Lovlina Borgohain and Parveen Hooda end 12-year wait for a women's Asian Games boxing gold. Ankush Panghal completes a golden hat-trick for Indian boxing at the Asian Games on Friday. He defeated South Korea’s Minseong Kim in the men's 80kg final.

Article Title: Sujeet Kalkal wins India's first wrestling gold at Asian Games 2026
Article Text:
Sujeet Kalkal (Image credit: X)

Dominant run to the final

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Beat Olympic champion

Eight straight points for gold

NEW DELHI: Sujeet Kalkal ended India's wait for a wrestling gold at the Asian Games 2026 with a stunning comeback in the men's freestyle 65kg category on Friday.The 23-year-old Indian defeated Tajikistan's Abdulmazhid Kudiyev 10-9 in a dramatic final at the Nagoya City Inae Sports Center.Kalkal was trailing 2-9 for most of the bout and looked set to miss out on the gold. But he produced a remarkable late fightback, scoring eight points in a row to turn the match around and seal India's first wrestling gold at the Games.Kalkal had already beaten tough opponents from Afghanistan, Iran and Japan on his way to the final.He began his campaign against Afghanistan's Sayed Omar Zazai and fell 0-3 behind early. Kalkal then changed the match with a push-out and a shoulder throw to take a 5-3 lead.He added four more points with another throw and a roll before completing a 13-3 win by technical superiority to move into the quarterfinals.Kalkal then produced another clinical performance against Iran's Abbas Ebrahimzadehsavadkouhi. He won by technical superiority without conceding a single point.The biggest test came in the semifinal against Japan's Olympic champion Kotaro Kiyooka.Kalkal trailed 0-2 after the first period but fought back in the second.He scored three points while Kiyooka managed only one, leaving the bout tied 3-3.Kalkal won the contest on criteria to book his place in the final.Kudiyev made a strong start in the final and built a 9-2 lead. The Tajik wrestler appeared to be close to winning the gold, but Kalkal refused to give up.The Indian then produced a sensational finish, scoring eight points in a row to overturn the deficit and win 10-9.The victory gave Kalkal his first Asian Games gold medal and India's first wrestling gold at the 2026 Games.
Article Summary: Sujeet Kalkal wins India's first wrestling gold at the Asian Games 2026. The 23-year-old Indian defeated Tajikistan's Abdulmazhid Kudiyev 10-9 in a dramatic final at the Nagoya City Inae Sports Center. He was trailing 2-9 for most of the bout and looked set to miss out on the gold.

Article Title: ‘I wanted to quit boxing’: Lovlina Borgohain fights through tough year to script historic Asian Games gold
Article Text:
Gold medallist India's Lovlina Borgohain (PTI Photo)

From Paris heartbreak to Asiad glory

‘I am feeling very good’

‘You are confident, you are the best’

NEW DELHI: A year after questioning her future in boxing, Lovlina Borgohain found the perfect answer on Friday, winning Asian Games gold on her 29th birthday.The 29-year-old had contemplated walking away from boxing after returning empty-handed from the Paris Olympics. Two years later, after enduring a difficult phase and questioning her future in the sport, Lovlina stood on top of the podium at the Asian Games — becoming only the second Indian woman boxer after the legendary MC Mary Kom to win the continental gold.“I wanted to quit boxing. But I continued. I had to change the colour of my medal. It was very important. More important than that is that I continued,” Lovlina said after defeating China's Ziyi Bao 5-0 in the women's 75kg final.Lovlina had won an Olympic bronze at Tokyo 2020 but returned from Paris without a medal. She subsequently took a year-long break before making her return to international boxing.The comeback, however, was far from smooth. She exited the World Championships in the second round and later skipped the World Boxing Cup final. At the Commonwealth Games this year, she had to settle for silver — a result that left her dissatisfied.“It was a tough year for me,” she said. “I was not happy about winning the silver medal at the Commonwealth Games. But, there are a lot of things in an athlete's life: losses, injuries. You have to handle a lot of things. This gold medal was very important to me.”The gold in Japan completed a remarkable turnaround for the boxer from Assam, who had won silver at the previous Asian Games after losing to China's Li Qian.Lovlina held her nerve in a closely fought final against Bao. She edged the opening round 3-2 on the judges' scorecards before winning the second 4-1. She maintained her composure in the final round to secure another 4-1 verdict and complete a 5-0 victory.The triumph ended India's 12-year wait for a women's Asian Games boxing champion, with Mary Kom having won flyweight gold at the 2014 edition in Incheon.Lovlina, however, was still taking in the magnitude of her achievement.“That is how I continued. I am feeling good. I don't know how to celebrate my gold. It has just ended. I need some time to accept that I have won. I am feeling very good.”Lovlina said the journey had also been about overcoming self-doubt. Looking back at her younger self, she said she would remind herself of the ability she possessed.“I had no confidence at that time, so if I had the chance to talk to my younger self I would tell her, 'You are confident, you are the best'. Now, I have a medal in every competition.”Mental strength, she added, was crucial when facing high-quality opponents.“I think it is important to be mentally strong. If we think that we have to win, no one can defeat us.”Japan, meanwhile, has now delivered another major moment in Lovlina's career.“I have to be strong and win. I was very positive about everything. Japan is very lucky for me. I was always think about winning.”And when asked whom she would call first after winning the biggest title of her Asian Games career, there was little hesitation.“The first person I am going to call is my mum. She doesn't watch my matches because she's very worried,” she said.
Article Summary: Lovlina Borgohain won Asian Games gold on her 29th birthday. The 29-year-old defeated China's Ziyi Bao 5-0 in the women's 75kg final. The triumph ended India's 12-year wait for a women's Asian Games boxing champion.

Article Title: Asian Games 2026: India add sepaktakraw bronze as medal tally swells to 72
Article Text:
Representative image: India lost to Japan in men’s quadrant semifinal. (Pic credit: X)

India fall short against Japan

Six medals and counting on Friday

NEW DELHI: India added another bronze to their swelling medal tally at the Asian Games on Friday as their men’s sepaktakraw team bowed out in the semifinal at the Nagoya City Mizuho Park Gymnasium.India went down 0-2 to hosts Japan in a tightly contested men’s quadrant semifinal, losing 12-15 and 13-15. The defeat ended their campaign with a bronze medal, but the podium finish marked another significant addition to India’s medal haul at Aichi-Nagoya.The bronze was India’s sixth medal of the day and took the overall tally to 72 — 12 gold, 25 silver and 35 bronze.India stayed competitive throughout the semifinal but could not convert the crucial points in either set. Japan edged the opening set 15-12 before holding their nerve to win the second 15-13 and secure a place in the gold-medal match.The result meant India finished their sepaktakraw campaign with one bronze medal.India had entered the semifinals unbeaten after topping Group A. They secured their place in the last four with a 2-1 victory over Myanmar on Thursday, winning 10-15, 15-13, 15-7.Earlier in the group stage, India had beaten Laos before defeating Vietnam 2-0 (15-12, 15-9).Indonesia topped Group B.The sepaktakraw bronze came after a prolific start to Friday for India.Kumkum Mohod, Ankita Bhakat and Kirti Sharma won gold in the women’s recurve team event, while Kumkum and Dhiraj Bommadevara claimed silver in the mixed recurve team event.Nethra Kumanan added a bronze in the women’s dinghy, while Lovlina Borgohain won gold in the women’s 75kg boxing final. India’s men’s recurve team then secured another silver.With the sepaktakraw bronze, India reached 72 medals and still have several medal opportunities on Friday.Parveen Hooda and Ankush Panghal are set for boxing gold-medal bouts, while wrestler Sujeet will fight Abdulmazid Kudiev of Tajikistan for gold. India’s women’s hockey team will face China in the final, while Dipanshi will compete for wrestling bronze against Kazakhstan’s Zeinep Bayanova.
Article Summary: India lose 0-2 to hosts Japan in men’s sepaktakraw semifinal. Defeat ends India's campaign with a bronze medal, but is another significant addition to India's medal haul at Aichi-Nagoya. India's overall medal tally now stands at 72, with 12 gold, 25 silver and 35 bronze.

Article Title: After Asiad row, Manika set to return to domestic circuit after four years amid ranking uncertainty
Article Text:
Manika Batra (Image: IANS)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Four years after her last appearance in a domestic tournament, India’s leading paddler Manika Batra is set to return to the national circuit, with the 31-year-old entering the National Ranking Table Tennis Championships in Panchkula , Haryana, scheduled from Octo 6 to 13.TOI has learnt that Manika has officially submitted her entry for the tournament, which will mark her first domestic appearance since the Senior Nationals in Shillong in April 2022. Batra had then lost to Ayhika Mukherjee in the pre-quarterfinals.Her return assumes added significance after her omission from India’s main squad for the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya. Manika, who was ranked world No. 51 and was India’s second-highest ranked women’s player at the time, was named among the reserves after her absence from domestic competitions meant she did not have the national ranking points required under the selection criteria.Manika had questioned the selection process following her omission and sought clarity from the authorities, including the sports ministry and Indian Olympic Association. Her decision to re-enter the domestic circuit now comes as the sport looks towards the next Olympic qualification cycle and the 2028 Los Angeles Games.However, the Panchkula tournament is facing an unusual situation of its own. The newly appointed ad-hoc committee overseeing table tennis has withdrawn official ranking points from upcoming National Ranking tournaments following the suspension of the Table Tennis Federation of India (TTFI) on Aug12, it has been learnt.The development has created uncertainty for players who had planned their domestic schedules around the ranking events. Panchkula has attracted more than 2,800 entries, including several established international players such as Sreeja Akula, Diya Chitale, Syndrela Das, Payas Jain, Manav Thakkar, Manush Shah, Ankur Bhattacharya, G Sathiyan and Harmeet Desai.For many players, the issue is particularly relevant as the domestic calendar feeds into selection and ranking considerations. The withdrawal of ranking points means the Panchkula event will not carry the same significance for players seeking to improve their national standings.International player Ankur Bhattacharya said the change had come after players had already invested considerable time and resources in preparation.“We train day in and day out to perform at these national rankings. Taking away ranking points right before the tournament makes all our hard work, intense preparation, and severe financial investments meaningless. It feels like our careers are being toyed with,” he said.Youth player Suhana Saini also said the uncertainty had made planning difficult.“This decision is a massive setback for all players, especially those trying to improve their standings before the international cycles. We are completely stranded and cannot plan our schedule. It is incredibly demotivating for the entire player community,” she said.Members of the table tennis fraternity have also sought clarity on the timing of the decision, coming nearly two months after the TTFI suspension.With the 2027 Olympic qualification cycle approaching and a packed international calendar ahead, including the Asian Championship, WTT Feeder Chennai, ITTF Mixed Team World Cup and World Youth Championship, players are keen for greater certainty over the domestic pathway.For Manika, meanwhile, Panchkula represents a return to the domestic circuit, one that could assume importance as she looks ahead to the next phase of her international career.
Article Summary: Manika Batra set to return to the national circuit. The 31-year-old will enter the National Ranking Table Tennis Championships in Panchkula, Haryana. It will be her first domestic appearance since the Senior Nationals in Shillong in April 2022.

Article Title: ‘This is not cricket’: Gautam Gambhir questions Guwahati pitch after India chase 406 with ease
Article Text:
India's coach Gautam Gambhir, left, chats with captain Shubman Gill during a practice session. (AP Photo)

‘It’s not fair for the bowlers’

Gambhir backs exposure for young bowlers

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: India head coach Gautam Gambhir had little doubt about the entertainment value of Wednesday’s extraordinary run-fest in Guwahati, but he was far less impressed by the conditions that allowed both teams to score more than 400 runs.After West Indies posted 405 for seven, India chased down the target in just 43.3 overs, winning by eight wickets to seal the three-match ODI series 2-0. Shubman Gill smashed an unbeaten 223 off 133 balls, while Rohit Sharma scored 101 off 75 as India completed the highest successful run chase in their ODI history.Yet, for Gambhir, the remarkable numbers also highlighted a concern. He felt the pitch offered too little to the bowlers and called for a greater balance between bat and ball.“Look, if I have to be absolutely honest, I feel I think there has to be a bit of more contest between bat and ball, because I think you talk about cricket - but this is not cricket, this is only batting,” Gambhir told Star Sports after the match.“Because imagine a young bowler bowling on this wicket, and the opposition getting 400 and then we go on to chase 400. Obviously, for the records it's outstanding, for the crowd it's outstanding, for the broadcaster it's outstanding, but if you ask me as a genuine cricket fan and as a coach, because I have to have sympathy for the bowlers as well.”“When you bowl on this kind of a wicket, it's not fair for the bowlers. So we've got to give something to the bowlers so there's at least something which the bowlers can work with,” he added.The Guwahati surface produced a stunning batting display, with West Indies reaching 405 for seven before India responded with 406 for two.John Campbell, Shai Hope and Amir Jangoo struck centuries for West Indies, while Gill and Rohit then led the Indian chase. Gill's unbeaten 223 was the defining innings of the day, while his opening partnership of 255 with Rohit was India's second-highest in men's ODIs. Virat Kohli , who had scored a century in the first ODI, contributed 29 off 19 balls before falling, while Ruturaj Gaikwad made 31 off 37.The match became only the second successful chase of a target of 400 or more in men's ODI history, after South Africa's famous 438-run chase against Australia in 2006.For Gambhir, however, the scale of the scoring made it important to consider what the conditions meant for the bowlers rather than simply celebrating the batting numbers.“The first thing is that you need some sympathy and a bit of margin for the bowlers,” he said.“Often you can't be hard on bowlers, because sometimes bowling figures are such that they haven't bowled as poorly as their figures suggest. Because the margin is very small.”He also pointed to the restrictions modern-day bowlers face in ODI cricket, including fielding restrictions, two new balls and the increasing power of batters.“Plus, I think you can only bowl in good areas because besides that, with five fielders inside, two new balls, and the kind of power-hitting there is now, bowlers don't really have many options,” Gambhir said.“That is why, as a coach, as a support staff, the first thing you look at is, were they able to execute their bowling or their plans properly? If they were able to do that, then you shouldn't be hard on them.”“If you get too hard just looking at their analysis, then we will never be able to develop bowlers.”India gave Auqib Nabi his ODI debut despite already leading the series 1-0, and Gambhir said putting inexperienced bowlers into difficult situations was an important part of India's preparation for the 2027 ODI World Cup.“Imagine Auqib [Nabi] playing his first game... somewhere you need to give them a bit of support and keep a bit of an extra cushion or extra options for them,” he said. “But unfortunately, today there wasn't much for any bowler.”Gambhir said India could have waited until the third ODI, when the series would already be decided, to give Nabi an opportunity. But he argued that a dead rubber would not recreate the pressure young players could experience at a World Cup.“We could have given Auqib a chance in the next match too when it's a dead rubber, but in a dead rubber, you don't have that pressure which comes with the pressure of winning a series,” he said.“And we all know that the World Cup is all about pressure. Cricket isn't going to change like that, only the pressure will be different because the World Cup comes once in four years, so we want to put bowlers under pressure.”He also cited Gurnoor Brar as an example of a young bowler who could benefit from being exposed to demanding phases of an ODI.“For example, Gurnoor [Brar]. Having Gurnoor bowl in the first 10 overs, bowling at the death, I know people will talk about his analysis, but the more he bowls in tough conditions, in tough situations, the better it is for Indian cricket,” Gambhir said.“Because you can have him bowl in the middle overs and get good analysis or good stats for him, make him bowl defensively, but the more we expose them at such times, the better it is for Indian cricket.”
Article Summary: India coach Gautam Gambhir unhappy with conditions in Guwahati. Both West Indies and India scored more than 400 runs in Wednesday's match. India chased down the target in 43.3 overs to win by eight wickets. Shubman Gill hit an unbeaten 223 as India won the match by eight runs.

Article Title: India’s new-ball puzzle: West Indies series offers young pacers a chance to stake claim
Article Text:

Kohli’s happy-hunting ground

Guwahati: With the ODI World Cup in South Africa just a year away, the Indian team management’s priority now is to identify the bowling combinations. A big part of the process is trying out different new-ball bowlers in the ongoing ODI series against West Indies.“You may see different bowlers taking the new ball because it is important for us to assess how these young players respond under pressure,” spin bowling coach Sairaj Bahutule said on the eve of the second ODI.It may be noted that India don’t have the services of Jasprit Bumrah for this series as he is part of the T20I team currently in the Asian Games in Japan.In the first ODI in Thiruvananthapuram, India opened the bowling with seam-bowling allrounder Nitish Kumar Reddy and Prasidh Krishna after benching Mohammed Siraj. Reddy’s only over with the new ball, however, yielded 18 runs.The team management must continue working on creating backup resources for the injury-prone Bumrah and Hardik Pandya.Bahutule stressed that identifying the right pace attack for South African conditions remains a key objective over the next 12 months.“We are aware of the type of pitches we’re likely to encounter in South Africa. The focus is on identifying players who can have the most impact in those conditions,” he added.The experiments are likely to continue.“These series are a good opportunity for us to see different combinations. We want to understand which bowlers can operate effectively in different phases of the innings,” Bahutule said.One bowler who has already strengthened his case is Kuldeep Yadav. The left-arm wrist-spinner produced another match-winning display in the opening ODI, ensuring India stayed in control.Bahutule described Kuldeep as “a match-winner for India” and praised both his work ethic and ability to deliver in any conditions. Kuldeep is expected to compete for the lead spinner’s spot in the XI when India reach South Africa for the World Cup.There are fewer concerns on the batting front. One may expect another run feast on Wednesday.Kohli has played two ODIs at the Barsapara Cricket Stadium, scored two centuries and walked away as the Player of the Match on both occasions.Justin Greaves, who scored a century in the first ODI, has been ruled out with a calf injury.
Article Summary: Kuldeep Yadav is expected to compete for the lead spinner’s spot in the XI when India reach South Africa for the World Cup. Justin Greaves, who scored a century in the first ODI, has been ruled out with a calf injury. Jasprit Bumrah is part of the T20I team currently in the Asian Games in Japan.

Article Title: 33 teams, no relegation, 198 matches: Mumbai football's Elite Division raises eyebrows
Article Text:
MFA Elite Division raises eyebrows

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

MUMBAI: Mumbai’s top-flight football league is set to enter a season of unprecedented proportions, and not necessarily for the right reasons.The Mumbai Football Association’s (MFA) Elite Division, which kicks off on Oct 15, will feature 33 teams, a number virtually unheard of for a top division. What’s more, there will be no relegation for three years. At the end of that period, the division could have as many as 39 teams.The bloated league is the result of the MFA’s decision to merge its Private and Corporate leagues. The Corporate league had complained of being treated as a second-class competition, with poor scheduling and matches often confined to barely three months, making it difficult for companies such as Western Railway and Indian Navy to commit teams. Rather than address those concerns, the MFA opted for a merger.The 33 teams will be split into three groups of 11, with the top four from each advancing to a playoff stage comprising two groups of six. The top four will then enter the semifinals and final. In all, 198 matches will need to be staged.But venues and scheduling pose another concern. While the MFA is fighting to retain the Neville D’Souza ground, it has secured Cooperage for matches.At time slots of 10 am and 12 noon! When Mumbai’s heat and humidity are at their peak. AFC A-licensed coach Raj Shekar told TOI: “We must consider Mumbai’s heat and humidity and whether this is sustainable for players, clubs and spectators if we want to make the league popular.Shekar also questioned the 51.5% increase in the entry fee, saying it had, to his understanding, neither been approved by the president nor placed before the executive committee.Ex-India captain Godfrey Pereira was blunt: “It’s an absolute mess and definitely not something that should happen. How will it help grow the sport? Without relegation, what’s there to fight? The quality will deteriorate.”Sudhakar Rane, MFA secretary, told TOI that it’s the best they could do. “Teams in the corporate league were complaining, so we thought that this was the best solution. About the ground, these slots were the only ones available so there’s nothing we can do about it.”
Article Summary: Mumbai's top-flight football league is set to enter a season of unprecedented proportions. The Mumbai Football Association’s (MFA) Elite Division, which kicks off on Oct 15, will feature 33 teams. There will be no relegation for three years. At the end of that period, the division could have as many as 39 teams.

NEW DELHI: India continued their strong run in archery at the Asian Games 2026 as the trio of Kushal Dalal, Sahil Jadhav and Ganesh Mani Ratnam won the gold medal in the men's compound team event in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, on Wednesday.The Indian team defeated China 238-237 in a thrilling final to clinch the gold medal.India held their nerve in a closely fought contest.The men's compound team gold came on a big day for Indian archery.Earlier, the women's compound team of Jyothi Surekha Vennam, Chikitha Taniparthi and Prithika Pradeep also won gold after beating China 238-234 in the final.India's compound mixed team of Chikitha and Sahil also finished on top after beating South Korea in a shoot-off. The victory also secured an Olympic quota place for India for the Los Angeles 2028 Games, where the compound mixed team event will make its Olympic debut.The men's team of Dalal, Jadhav and Ganesh had earlier defeated the UAE 235-215 in the round of 16 and Bhutan 235-232 in the quarterfinals.The Indian women's and mixed teams successfully defended the compound team titles won at the previous Asian Games in Hangzhou.

Article Title: 'Real-life hero': Sachin Tendulkar, Yuvraj Singh lead cricket fraternity in hailing Captain Smit Machchhar after saving 174 lives

Smit Machchhar

'A true real-life hero': Sachin Tendulkar

Raina hails 'son of Gujarat'

Sehwag praises his courage under pressure

Yuvraj: 'Some moments show you what a person is truly made of'

NEW DELHI: The courage of Indian pilot Captain Smit Machchhar, who was seriously injured while trying to prevent a potential catastrophe aboard flydubai Flight FZ1073, has earned admiration from across the country, including some of India's biggest cricketing names.Sachin Tendulkar, Yuvraj Singh, Suresh Raina and Virender Sehwag were among the former India cricketers who took to social media to salute Machchhar for his bravery and presence of mind during the terrifying mid-air incident.Machchhar was the captain of the Dubai-to-Tel Aviv flight when a violent confrontation reportedly broke out in the cockpit on Wednesday. According to reports, he was attacked by his co-pilot but, despite suffering serious injuries, managed to help open the cockpit door, allowing passengers and crew members to intervene. The aircraft was subsequently diverted and landed safely in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia. All 174 people aboard were reported safe.Tendulkar was among the first prominent cricketers to acknowledge Machchhar's courage."Learnt about the incredible bravery of Captain Smit Machchhar. Immense courage in the face of a terrifying and unprecedented challenge. A true real-life hero. The entire world is proud of you," Tendulkar wrote.Former India batter Suresh Raina also paid tribute to Machchhar, highlighting the captain's courage despite being seriously injured."A true hero, a proud moment for India! Salute to Captain Smit Machchhar, a son of Gujarat, whose extraordinary courage and presence of mind, even while seriously injured, helped save 174 precious lives," Raina wrote.Virender Sehwag highlighted the extraordinary circumstances in which Machchhar continued to act despite his injuries."In the face of the gravest danger and despite being seriously injured, he showed immense courage and an unwavering resolve to protect the lives of others," Sehwag wrote.Yuvraj Singh also joined the tributes, focusing on Machchhar's decision to put the safety of others ahead of his own."Some moments show you what a person is truly made of," Yuvraj wrote.Machchhar, who has more than 13 years of commercial flying experience and previously worked with SpiceJet before joining flydubai in 2022, is currently recovering after undergoing treatment in Saudi Arabia.
Article Summary: Captain Smit Machchhar was seriously injured while trying to prevent a potential catastrophe aboard flydubai Flight FZ1073. Sachin Tendulkar, Yuvraj Singh, Suresh Raina and Virender Sehwag took to social media to pay tribute to the pilot's bravery. All 174 people aboard the flight were reported safe.

Article Title: India vs Pakistan final: What happens if rain washes out Asian Games gold medal clash?
Article Text:
India's Jasprit Bumrah, third right, celebrates with teammates (PTI Photo)

What happens if rain washes out India vs Pakistan final?

India enter final after dominant semi-final

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

India and Pakistan are set to battle for the men's cricket gold medal at the 2026 Asian Games , but persistent rain in Nisshin could throw a major twist into Saturday's summit clash.India booked their place in the final with a commanding 124-run win over Sri Lanka in the semi-final. After being asked to bat, Shreyas Iyer 's side posted 169/7 in 20 overs before Jasprit Bumrah , Axar Patel and Abhishek Sharma claimed two wickets each to bowl Sri Lanka out for just 45.The victory guaranteed India at least a silver medal, but the team will now be hoping the weather does not prevent them from competing for gold against arch-rivals Pakistan.The weather forecast in Nisshin could be a concern. According to AccuWeather, there is a 62% chance of rain in the morning on Saturday, with the probability expected to fall to 25% in the afternoon. The temperature is likely to remain around 20 degrees Celsius, while cloud cover is expected to be about 37%.If rain prevents the final from producing a result, the rules for the 2026 Asian Games are different from those used at the previous edition.At the 2023 Asian Games in Hangzhou, India's men's team won the gold medal after the final against Afghanistan was washed out. India were declared champions because they were the higher-ranked T20I side.That rule does not apply in Nisshin.Under the regulations for the ongoing edition, if the final is abandoned without a result, the gold medal will be shared by India and Pakistan.Both finalists would therefore be declared joint gold medallists.India's route to the final was emphatic. Iyer and Co. recovered to post 169/7 after being sent in by Sri Lanka, with Ishan Kishan playing a key role in the innings.The bowlers then made short work of the Sri Lankan chase. Bumrah, Axar and Abhishek picked up two wickets apiece as Sri Lanka were dismissed for 45, giving India a 124-run victory.Pakistan also reached the final after winning their semi-final, setting up the first meeting between the two sides in the men's cricket competition at the Asian Games.For India, the stakes are particularly significant. They are the defending champions and have brought a full-strength team to Japan, including pace spearhead Bumrah. A victory would allow them to retain the gold medal they won at Hangzhou.But if the rain has the final say and no result is possible, neither side will take gold outright. The 2026 Asian Games rules mean India and Pakistan will share the gold medal.
Article Summary: India beat Sri Lanka by 124 runs in the semi-final of the men's cricket competition at the 2026 Asian Games in Nisshin. Jasprit Bumrah, Axar Patel and Abhishek Sharma claimed two wickets each as India bowled Sri Lanka out for just 45. If the final is abandoned without a result, the gold medal will be shared by India and Pakistan.

Article Title: ‘Unfinished business’: Shubman Gill eyes 2027 ODI World Cup redemption, values Virat Kohli-Rohit Sharma experience
Article Text:
India captain Shubman Gill (AFP Photo)

‘It is unfinished business’

Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli (ANI Photo)

‘Extremely lucky’ to have Virat and Rohit

No. 1 ranking takes a back seat

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Shubman Gill has already started looking towards the 2027 ODI World Cup, and for India's captain, the tournament represents more than another opportunity on the global stage. It is unfinished business.Gill, the world's No. 1-ranked ODI batter, reflected on India's heartbreaking end to the 2023 World Cup campaign and the significance of getting another chance to compete for the biggest prize in ODI cricket. Speaking to JioStar ahead of the third ODI against the West Indies, Gill also underlined the value of having two vastly experienced campaigners — Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma — around him as he grows into his leadership role.India had gone through the 2023 World Cup unbeaten in the league stage and entered the final against Australia as the tournament's standout side before suffering a six-wicket defeat in Ahmedabad.For Gill, that painful ending still carries significance."Yes, absolutely, it's unfinished business because of the way we played throughout that World Cup. We were looking like the best team in the tournament. But World Cups are like that. You might play the entire tournament well, but you don't play one game well, and that game could be the final of the World Cup," Gill told JioStar.The India captain also highlighted how limited the opportunities are for a player to compete in a World Cup, making every appearance particularly precious."So definitely, it is unfinished business. And as a player, you don't get that many opportunities to represent your country in a World Cup. There could be two, three, four, five, you never know. So, every World Cup that you play for your country is a big honour. So, very grateful to be able to play another one."The 2027 edition will therefore carry an added significance for a young India side that will enter the tournament with Gill at the helm and a mix of emerging players and established stars.While Gill is increasingly assuming responsibility as captain, he is also benefiting from the presence of two of India's most experienced ODI players.Kohli and Rohit remain important figures in the dressing room, and Gill believes their experience can be invaluable as India prepare for another World Cup campaign."I feel extremely lucky. Virat bhai is probably the best ODI batter, and Rohit bhai is the best ODI opener in the world. And then to be able to have these two players in the team and their experience, and the moments that they have shared together, it's great, and we really enjoy having them in the team. And their experience is very valuable for us," he said.For Gill, learning from senior players is not restricted to Kohli and Rohit. He also seeks the views of other experienced members of the squad before making decisions on the field."Often, not just those two; I go to even KL or Shreyas, for that matter. I like to take everyone's opinion," Gill said.He explained that captaincy, for him, involves listening to different perspectives before deciding what he believes will work best in a particular situation."But most of the time, it happens that if they come to suggest something, then I might have thought about it. If I haven't thought about it, then I'll think about what their thoughts are, what their opinions are. So, you listen to everyone, see what they are thinking, and then what, according to me, would work best in that situation; I think learning comes from that."Gill's own evolution has been rapid. He is currently the No. 1-ranked ODI batter, a position he first reached during the 2023 World Cup.While becoming the world's top-ranked ODI batter was once a personal ambition, Gill now places greater emphasis on what his performances contribute to the team."The first time when I became the number one-ranked batsman, I think it was during the 2023 World Cup. And it felt good. As a kid, you look at the rankings, so it was like a tick mark that, 'Okay, once I want to become the number one-ranked ODI batsman.' So it feels good, but I think right now it doesn't matter as much. For me, it's more important that if you step out in a match, go to bat, then how you can make the team win, how you can contribute," he said.That shift in perspective is also reflected in how Gill views captaincy. Rather than treating the role as a burden, he sees it as a responsibility entrusted to him."I look at it more like a responsibility. Even while growing up, it was not really my dream that I had to become India's captain one day. My dream was always to play for the country and win matches for my country, and that was always my aim growing up," he said."So, when I got this opportunity to captain, obviously, it was a big honour and a big responsibility. And I look at it as I have been given the responsibility of the team, and that makes things a lot easier for me. I don't feel that much pressure about this thing because I feel that if I do things with the right intent, then everything will fall into place."
Article Summary: India captain Shubman Gill has already started looking towards the 2027 ODI World Cup. Gill, the world's No. 1-ranked ODI batter, reflected on India's heartbreaking end to the 2023 World Cup campaign. Gill also underlined the value of having two vastly experienced campaigners — Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma.

Article Title: ‘She would be sitting on the bench again’: Gujarat Giants explain Danni Wyatt-Hodge release
Article Text:
England's Danni Wyatt-Hodge celebrates reaching her century. (AP Photo)

Titas release

Fast-bowling depth

Giants target bowling consistency

Anushka, Happy in focus

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Mumbai: Gujarat Giants retained a large chunk of their squad ahead of the 2027 Women's Premier League player auction, a departure from the second season when they released 11 players. But they surprised by letting go of England batter Danni Wyatt-Hodge, who finished as the top run-scorer in the 2026 Women's T20 World Cup in England.Wyatt-Hodge scored 302 runs in seven matches at 60.40, including a century and two fifties, at a strike rate of 149.50, helping England reach the final.Gujarat Giants head coach Michael Klinger said Wyatt-Hodge was released because she was likely to spend much of WPL 2027 on the bench, with England also having commitments during the tournament."As you would have seen last year, she didn't quite fit into our four overseas lineup for the majority of the time. I felt for her. She came in for one game and started reasonably well, getting about 12 or 15. Then she got sick just before the next game and was left out. Georgia Wareham came back in and had a really good game, and we stuck with that middle order all round option."This year, England have commitments during the WPL. If we went with a similar setup, she would probably be sitting on the bench again. I spoke to both her and her representative, and they are keen for her to play some cricket during that time, leading into the Champions Trophy.I'm not sure whether she will enter the auction, but she was quite keen to play that England series around the same time. So for both parties, this was the best way to go. It also gives us another option in the auction, either the same skill set or a different one," Klinger said at an interaction on Thursday.Klinger said injury concerns also contributed to the decision to release India pacer Titas Sadhu, who has played 20 white-ball internationals."What probably went against her this time was her injuries. She had an injury last season where we didn't really get a chance to see her, and she has been injured since. She is just making her comeback now."We are having a training camp at the moment and we still asked her to come so we could have a look at her before the auction. She is progressing well and will start the domestic season on the 26th of October. Releasing her gives us a few more options in the auction. There is no reason we may not look to get her back, but it also gives us a chance to look at other options," he said.Klinger believes India's domestic fast-bowling pool has improved, though the real test will come against international batters.“Overall, domestically, I think fast bowling is the area where Indian cricket can keep building depth. There has been a big change from when I started in this role a few years ago. The fast bowlers around the country are physically better. When you watch them bowl and field, they are fitter, more versatile, move better and are more agile."That is only going to help them maintain pace and aggression for longer periods without injury. So I think Indian cricket is definitely on the right track in building depth in fast bowling. The test is always when they come up against international batters, whether that's international Indian batters or overseas batters in the WPL, because a lot of these bowlers haven't done that before. That's always the biggest test when they get on the big stage,” Klinger said.After missing the playoffs in their first two seasons, Gujarat Giants have reached the knockout stage in the last two. Klinger, who is overseeing an off-season camp in Bengaluru ahead of the October 28 auction in Kochi, identified bowling consistency as an area for improvement."To be honest, we just had a bad final against Delhi Capitals. We beat them twice during the season in close games and didn't bring our best in that eliminator. That was disappointing, because I felt we probably had a stronger season than DC did throughout the year. But that's what finals are about. You need your best players to step up, and we probably didn't.""I think we can get more consistency with our bowling. Looking at the data and statistical information from last season, that's one area where we can improve. We have the personnel, and a couple of players are putting their hand up to get opportunities there this year, which will help us get some more quality overs."Last year we defended some really big scores, but they were pretty tight games, and we also chased some big scores. I feel our batting is strong. If we can tighten up our bowling at certain times, then we'll be fine," he added.Klinger backed Anushka Sharma after her impressive first WPL season and said her experience of international cricket could provide extra motivation."Anushka Sharma was fantastic for us last year in her first WPL season. She has had a really good ODI series against Australia A and had a taste of international cricket. She probably could have been kept a little longer with more opportunities there, but I'm hoping that works in our favour."Having tasted international cricket, I'm sure she will be desperate to do everything she can to get back. Both she and Yastika (Bhatia, who too will play for GG in WPL-2027) are in the same boat, playing for India at the moment.I'm hoping they will have a lot of motivation to have a really good WPL and help break back into the Indian starting 11. That gives them great motivation, which can only help us as well."Klinger also identified young fast bowler Happy Kumari as a player to watch."One other I would mention, though it's hard to pinpoint because we have great skill sets throughout the squad, is Happy Kumari, a young fast bowler. We saw her progress and train really well for us last year. She got one opportunity in a match and has been working hard since. If she keeps progressing that way, she may get more games for us in this WPL. I'm looking forward to seeing her keep improving up until January," he concluded.
Article Summary: Gujarat Giants release Danni Wyatt-Hodge ahead of 2027 Women's Premier League auction. England batter scored 302 runs in seven matches at 60.40, including a century and two fifties, at a strike rate of 149.50. India pacer Titas Sadhu released due to injuries.

Article Title: India to open 2027 World Cup against Australia, face Pakistan on October 10
Article Text:
India's Virat Kohli and skipper Shubman Gill (ANI Photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

New Delhi: India will begin their 2027 ODI World Cup campaign against defending champions Australia in Cape Town on October 7, the International Cricket Council (ICC) announced in Cape Town on Thursday.The two finalists from the last edition will kick off the round-robin stage. The tournament will begin on October 2 with a three-match Super Series to determine two qualifiers.As has been the trend in ICC events over the last decade, India and Pakistan have been drawn in the same group and are slated to face each other on October 10 in Johannesburg. The 51-day tournament will conclude with the final in Johannesburg on November 21.India will get a two-day break before the match against Pakistan, who will play their opening match against Afghanistan in Tshwane on October 8.The 12 teams have been divided into two groups, with the top three from each group and the best fourth-placed team advancing to the Super 7 phase, followed by the two semifinals.Besides India, Australia and Pakistan, the other teams in Group A are Afghanistan and Zimbabwe, with one qualifier yet to be decided.Interestingly, the seedings for the Super 7 phase have been pre-decided on the basis of the ICC ODI rankings as of September 30, 2026. India, Australia and Pakistan are seeded A1, A2 and A3 respectively, while England are seeded AB4. New Zealand, South Africa and Sri Lanka are seeded B1, B2 and B3 respectively.Should a non-seeded team finish in a qualifying position above a pre-seeded team, it will assume the Super 7 position allocated to the pre-seeded team it has displaced.This has been done to make it easier for fans to plan their travel for the tournament.Group B features hosts South Africa, England, New Zealand, Sri Lanka and Bangladesh, along with the other qualifier.The Super 7 seedings will remain fixed irrespective of where the top three teams from each group finish in the first round. The ICC has understood to have adopted the system to make it easier for fans to plan their travel for the tournament.
Article Summary: India will begin their 2027 ODI World Cup campaign against defending champions Australia in Cape Town on October 7. The two finalists from the last edition will kick off the round-robin stage. The tournament will begin on October 2 with a three-match Super Series to determine two qualifiers. The 51-day tournament will conclude with the final in Johannesburg on November 21.

Article Title: ‘Where is the contest between bat and ball?’ 811-run IND vs WI Guwahati ODI raises questions
Article Text:
Shubman Gill

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

KOCHI: 811 runs were scored in 93.3 overs in the second ODI between India and West Indies at Guwahati on a ridiculous day of batting, when bowlers were reduced to mute spectators. Once, a match like this would have been celebrated like a historic event. Now, it’s just another game of cricket. A game like this doesn’t thrill the audience; it leaves them weary of watching another run-fest on a pitch described as a ‘national highway’ by Ravi Shastri on commentary.India captain Shubman Gill’s unbeaten 223 was sublime, his impeccable timing, placement and voracious appetite hallmarks of his talent. So too was Rohit Sharma’s easy-on-the-eye 101. The West Indies also had three centurions. These batters needed adversaries, and they found none. Not from the bowlers nor from the pitch.“Extremely boring game yaar,” Madan Lal, former medium-pacer and member of India’s 1983 World Cup-winning squad, told TOI.“Over 800 runs scored on a paata wicket and there was absolutely nothing in it for the bowlers. Give the bowlers something to play with. Where is the contest between bat and ball?" Lal observed.He reckons that an ideal ODI should end around 280 per side. The kind of game that offers a genuine contest and the one that spectators want to watch.For that to happen, he says the curators must put some life into these insipid wickets. “I don’t think that will happen,” he laments.Former Delhi pacer Sanjiv Sharma attributes the trend to the proliferation of T20Is and expects more teams to chase down 400+ scores in ODIs going forward.“In T20Is, we see teams chase down 200+ scores. Batters are carrying that confidence into the 50-over format,” he said.Lal points out that the real worry about such run-fests is that in the long term it kills the quality of bowling. Sharma concurred. “Apart from Kuldeep (Yadav), neither side had a match-winner with the ball. India had a second-string attack, but what about the West Indies? Their bowling was abysmal,” he added.One-day cricket is in an existential crisis in a calendar surfeit with T20Is. The lure of the 50-over game is that, unlike the T20Is, it gives time for a contest to build, turn and breathe. Gill’s second double hundred in this format will find its way into the record books, but a record without contest is mere arithmetic.

The International Cricket Council (ICC) on Thursday introduced several changes to the playing conditions in men's and women's cricket, including penalties for batters who waste time, tighter specifications for balls used in women's cricket, the option of pink balls in daytime Test matches and a rule change for the final over of a day's play.The changes will apply to all international series beginning on October 1 or later, while series that are already underway will continue under the existing regulations.The updated Playing Conditions for men and women across all formats incorporate changes to the MCC Laws of Cricket that come into effect on Thursday.The changes have been introduced to "address time-wasting, standardise ball specifications and clarify certain aspects of fielding."The playing condition for time-wasting by batters has been revised in men's cricket.If a batter is not ready to face the next delivery within the prescribed time, they will receive a warning for the first offence and a final warning for the second. A third offence, and every subsequent offence, will result in five penalty runs being awarded to the fielding team.Code of Conduct provisions may also be used if a batter repeatedly wastes time.The ICC has introduced tighter limits on the size and weight of balls used in women's international cricket.Men's cricket already has limited tolerances for ball size and weight. However, manufacturers have often produced one ball for both women's and junior cricket. The new rules introduce three separate size and weight specifications for men's, women's and junior cricket.A new men's ball must weigh between 5.5 and 5.75 ounces (156-163 grams) and measure 22.4-22.9 centimetres in circumference. For women's cricket, the ball must weigh 5-5.25 ounces (142-149 grams) and measure 21.5-22 centimetres in circumference.Following MCC recommendations, The ICC has also clarified what constitutes an overthrow.An overthrow is defined as an attempt to direct the ball towards the stumps to prevent runs or complete a run-out. A misfield, whether the fielder is trying to stop the ball or pass it to another fielder, will not be considered an overthrow.Umpires will now have greater discretion in deciding when a ball is "finally settled", which can be particularly important on the final delivery of a close match.The ball no longer has to be in the bowler's or wicketkeeper's hands for it to be considered finally settled.For a ball to be considered held by a fielder during a run-out or stumping, the fielder must have complete control of it.Simply touching the ball with a hand while it breaks the stumps will not be enough to establish that the ball was held.Pink balls may be used on a trial basis in daytime Test matches if both teams agree before the match. The change is aimed at reducing loss of playing time because of bad light.Once a Test begins with a pink ball, the decision cannot be changed and the pink ball must be used for the remainder of the match. A switch from a red ball to a pink ball after the start of the Test will not be allowed.The fall of a wicket during the final over of the day's play will no longer automatically bring the day's play to an end if the over has not been completed and weather and conditions allow play to continue.The ICC said the change was made because stopping at the fall of a wicket does not save time, as the remaining deliveries still have to be bowled the following day. The change will also reward the fielding team and keep the game going in such situations.T20Is will now have a fixed 15-minute interval. This can be reduced to a minimum of 10 minutes if playing time has been lost.The ODI and T20I playing conditions now allow the head coach or their designate to enter the field during drinks intervals.The trial for the leg-side wide rule has now been made permanent in ODI and T20I playing conditions.
Article Summary: The International Cricket Council (ICC) introduced several changes to the playing conditions in men's and women's cricket. The changes include penalties for batters who waste time, tighter specifications for balls used in women's international cricket, the option of pink balls in daytime Test matches and a change for the final over of a day's play.

Kolkata: Gurinder Singh Sangha, a Jalandhar-based international hockey umpire and technical official who was appointed by the Asian Hockey Federation (AHF) as umpire manager for the hockey competition at the 20th Asian Games in Nagoya, has left Japan before the tournament concluded following multiple complaints of alleged sexual misconduct against him.Sources alleged that Sangha misbehaved with a female hockey official from Malaysia.“On the pretext of mentoring and teaching her, he allegedly tried to hug her on multiple occasions and also kissed her. Following the incident, she complained to the Malaysian umpire manager,” a source familiar with the development said.Multiple sources also alleged that Sangha behaved inappropriately with a member of the hotel staff and showed her obscene videos in his room. However, TOI could not independently verify the allegation.The latest complaint is not the first allegation made against Sangha. During the Hockey India League in Ranchi in January 2025, a female umpire filed a formal complaint against him while he was serving as Umpires' Manager. Hockey India subsequently confirmed receipt of the complaint and constituted a three-member committee to conduct a preliminary investigation into the matter.According to the complaint, the female umpire alleged that Sangha's conduct during an interaction at the team hotel in Ranchi on January 20, 2025, was "unwanted and inappropriate" and left her uncomfortable. She urged Hockey India to take action and ensure a safe and respectful working environment for women officials.In a communication dated January 21, 2025, HI secretary general Bhola Nath Singh informed stakeholders that a three-member panel had been constituted in consultation with the federation's Internal Complaint Committee for Prevention of Sexual Harassment to carry out a preliminary investigation and submit its report within two days.The outcome of that inquiry could not be immediately ascertained. However, official documents show that the complaint was formally received by Hockey India and referred for investigation.The latest episode comes amid increased scrutiny of misconduct complaints within Indian hockey. Earlier this year, Hockey India removed a support staff member from a national camp after harassment allegations surfaced against him, stating that action was taken immediately after the matter came to its notice.The federation has also grappled with other complaints in recent times, including an April 2026 complaint alleging sexual harassment and abuse of authority by a Hockey India official, and a 2025 case involving a junior women's team coach.During the inaugural Women's Hockey India League, a coach was removed overnight after authorities were informed of harassment complaints involving younger players.
Article Summary: Gurinder Singh Sangha was appointed as umpire manager for the hockey competition at the 20th Asian Games in Nagoya. He has left Japan before the tournament concluded following multiple complaints of alleged sexual misconduct against him.Sources alleged that Sangha misbehaved with a female hockey official from Malaysia.

Article Title: Asian Games: India add another archery silver as men’s recurve team loses to South Korea
Article Text:
India's Dhiraj Bommadevara reacts with Neeraj Chauhan. (Reuters Photo)

India pushed Korea in opening set

Another big day for Indian archery

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: India's men's recurve team added another silver medal to the country's growing archery haul at the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, losing 1-5 to South Korea in the gold-medal match on Friday. Dhiraj Bommadevara , Yashdeep Bhoge and Neeraj Chauhan were unable to overcome the formidable Korean trio, but their silver ensured another medal for India on a memorable day for the archers.It was India's third archery medal on Friday, taking the country's overall tally in the sport at the Asian Games to seven — four gold, two silver and one bronze.The silver also matched India's finish in the men's recurve team event from the previous edition in Hangzhou.India made an encouraging start to the final, shooting 29 with their opening three arrows and putting the pressure on Korea.The Koreans responded with an identical 29, taking the set to 56 after six arrows. India needed 28 from their final three arrows to win the set outright, but an 8 from one of their archers left them short. The set ended level, with both teams taking one point as India and Korea moved to 1-1.Korea then produced a stunning start to the second set, hitting a perfect 30 from their opening three arrows.India, by contrast, managed only 25 from their first three shots and were immediately under pressure. The Indian trio managed to post 50 overall, but Korea finished on 57 to take the set and move 3-1 ahead.India needed a strong response in the third set to stay alive in the contest.They began with 28 from their opening three arrows, with Korea matching that score to keep the set finely poised. However, Neeraj's 7 with his second arrow put India on the back foot. Dhiraj produced a crucial 10 with India's final arrow to take the team's score to 54, but Korea remained composed and finished on 56 to seal the gold medal.India eventually lost the contest 1-5 and had to settle for silver.The men's team had booked its place in the final earlier in the day with a commanding 6-0 victory over Iran in the semifinal.Dhiraj, Yashdeep and Neeraj defeated Mohammadhossein Golshani, Sadegh Ashrafi and Reza Shabani 58-53, 56-53, 56-55.Korea had also produced a dominant semifinal performance, blanking Chinese Taipei 6-0 to set up the final against India.The men's silver came after an extraordinary morning session for Indian archery.Ankita Bhakat, Kirti Sharma and 17-year-old Kumkum Mohod stunned 10-time Olympic champions South Korea 5-3 to win India's maiden Asian Games gold in the women's recurve team event.Later, Kumkum and Dhiraj added another silver after China defeated them 5-3 in the mixed team recurve final.India's four archery gold medals have come in the men's compound, women's compound, mixed compound and women's recurve team events.With the men's recurve silver and mixed recurve silver added to the tally, India now have seven archery medals — four gold, two silver and one bronze — in Aichi-Nagoya.
Article Summary: India's men's recurve team loses 1-5 to South Korea in the gold-medal match. It was India's third archery medal on Friday, taking the country's overall tally in the sport to seven. India now have seven archery medals — four gold, two silver and one bronze.

Article Title: Asian Games: Nethra Kumanan ends long wait for maiden sailing medal with bronze
Article Text:
Nethra Kumanan (ANI Photo)

Fourth time lucky for Nethra

Vishnu misses out despite strong finish

NEW DELHI: India's Nethra Kumanan finally broke her Asian Games medal jinx on Friday, clinching bronze in the women's dinghy event at the Aichi-Nagoya Games to secure her first medal at the continental showpiece in her fourth appearance.The 29-year-old Chennai sailor, a two-time Olympian, finished third with 14 points overall — seven from the qualification races and seven from the final — behind Thailand's Sophia Montgomery, who won gold with five points, and Singapore's Jania Ang, who took silver with 13.In sailing, lower scores are better, with competitors awarded points corresponding to their finishing position in each race. The sailor with the lowest aggregate score wins the regatta.Nethra had entered the final day with the medal within reach and delivered when it mattered. She finished sixth in one of the two final races before winning the other to strengthen her position on the podium.The bronze was particularly significant for Nethra, who had endured heartbreak at previous editions of the Asian Games.She had competed at the 2014, 2018 and 2022 editions but narrowly missed out on a medal twice, finishing fourth on both occasions.Her persistence finally paid off in Aichi-Nagoya as she converted another strong campaign into a podium finish.Nethra's medal also added to India's growing sailing haul at the Games.India had already secured two sailing medals before Friday's competition. Manu Francis and Prince Noble won silver in the men's skiff event on Thursday, while Harshita Tomar and Shital Verma claimed bronze in the women's skiff competition.The women's skiff medal came after India initially finished fourth, with the position upgraded following China's disqualification.There was disappointment for India's Vishnu Saravanan in the men's dinghy event as the Olympian finished fourth.Saravanan ended his final two races strongly, finishing second in both, but an accumulated qualification score of 17 left him with 21 points overall and outside the medal positions.South Korea's Jeemin Ha won gold with nine points, Hong Kong China's Nicholas Halliday took silver with 11, while Malaysia's Mohd Khairulnizam finished third with 14.Saravanan had won bronze at the previous Asian Games.
Article Summary: Nethra Kumanan wins bronze in women's dinghy event at Aichi-Nagoya Games. It is the 29-year-old Chennai sailor's first medal at Asian Games in her fourth appearance. India's Vishnu Saravanan misses out on medal despite finishing fourth.

Article Title: Asian Games: Birthday girl Lovlina Borgohain makes history with gold, joins Mary Kom in elite club
Article Text:
India's Lovlina Borgohain celebrates after winning a gold-medal bout against China's Ziyi Bao. (PTI Photo)

Lovlina holds nerve in tight final

India's Lovlina Borgohain celebrates after winning against China's Bao Ziyi. (Reuters Photo)

From silver in Hangzhou to historic gold

NEW DELHi: Birthday girl Lovlina Borgohain gave herself the perfect gift on Friday, scripting history by becoming only the second Indian woman boxer to win an Asian Games gold medal after the legendary MC Mary Kom The 29-year-old Indian defeated China's Ziyi Bao 5-0 in a closely contested women's 75kg final in Aichi-Nagoya to finally add the Asian Games gold to the silver she won at the previous edition.Lovlina's triumph also ended a wait that began in Hangzhou, where she had reached the final but lost to another Chinese boxer, Li Qian, to settle for silver.On Friday, however, there was no denying her.The Indian made a confident start to the final, edging the opening round 3-2 on the judges' scorecards. Bao responded with an aggressive approach in the second, forcing Lovlina into a more defensive mode as the two boxers engaged in a series of exchanges in the middle of the ring.Despite the pressure, Lovlina remained composed and finished the round strongly. She won it 4-1 to stretch her overall advantage to 2-0 heading into the final round.With the gold within touching distance, Lovlina produced another controlled performance in the third.She again won the round 4-1 to complete a comprehensive 5-0 verdict and claim the biggest title of her Asian Games career.The victory was particularly significant given the quality of opposition she had overcome on her way to the final.In the semifinal, Lovlina edged reigning 70kg world champion Natalya Bogdanova of Kazakhstan 3-2 in another closely fought contest.In the semis, Lovlina had struggled to find her rhythm in the opening round against Bogdanova and went behind 2-3 on the judges' cards. She changed gears in the second, becoming more aggressive and landing cleaner punches to dominate the round 5-0.Bogdanova came forward again in the decider, while Lovlina relied on her defence and counter-attacks. The Kazakh edged the round 3-2, but Lovlina's advantage from the second round proved decisive.She secured the split-decision victory after three of the five judges scored the bout in her favour, booking her place in a second successive Asian Games final.That achievement had already made Lovlina the first Indian woman boxer to reach back-to-back Asian Games finals. Her gold on Friday now puts her alongside Mary Kom, who won the women's flyweight gold at the 2014 Asian Games in Incheon.India's boxing campaign has already surpassed its medal tally from Hangzhou. The country had won four medals at the 2023 edition, including one silver and three bronze. This time, Indian boxers have already secured six medals, with two more gold-medal opportunities remaining on Friday.Parveen Hooda will fight for gold in the 65kg category, while Ankush Panghal will contest the 80kg final later in the day.
Article Summary: Lovlina Borgohain becomes only the second Indian woman boxer to win an Asian Games gold medal after the legendary MC Mary Kom. The 29-year-old Indian defeated China's Ziyi Bao 5-0 in a closely contested women's 75kg final.

Article Title: Asian Games 2026: Kumkum Mohod, Dhiraj Bommadevara win mixed recurve team silver
Article Text:
India's Kumkum Anil Mohod and Dhiraj Bommadevara. (Reuters Photo)

India fight back from 0-4 down

Dramatic semifinal comeback against Japan

NEW DELHI: Kumkum Mohod and Dhiraj Bommadevara signed off with a silver medal in the mixed team recurve event after China’s Jingyi Zhu and Mengqi Li prevailed 5-3 in a closely fought gold-medal match at the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya on Friday.The Indian pair had to settle for silver after fighting back from a 0-4 deficit and briefly threatening to take the contest into a deciding shoot-off. Their medal was India’s sixth in archery at the Games, taking the discipline’s tally to four gold, one silver and one bronze.China made the stronger start, with Dhiraj opening with an 8 before Kumkum followed with a 7. India managed 34 points in the opening set, while Zhu and Li combined for 38 to take the first two match points.India then found itself in a deeper hole in the second set. Kumkum and Dhiraj could manage only 35, while China posted 37 to win the set and move 4-0 ahead.With China needing just one more set to claim gold, India produced a determined response.Kumkum opened the third set with an 8 but responded with a crucial 10 on her second attempt. Dhiraj helped India post 37, while China finished on 36. Li's final arrow was a 7, leaving the door open for India.The result gave India the set, crucially, they remained alive in the match at 2-4.Kumkum and Dhiraj then produced one of their best shots of the final in the fourth set. Kumkum began with a 9 and Dhiraj followed with another 9 to give India 18 points from the opening two arrows.Kumkum then delivered a 10 before Dhiraj added a 9, taking India to 37. China, however, held its nerve and Zhu and Li matched India's score, with a 10 on their final arrow levelling the set at 37-37.That was enough for China to secure the one point required for gold, leaving India with the silver.Kumkum and Dhiraj had earlier produced a superb comeback to defeat Japan's Nanami Asakuno and Junya Nakanishi 5-3 in the semifinal.India trailed 0-2 after losing the opening set 37-38. The second set ended 36-36, leaving Japan 3-1 ahead, but the Indian pair responded strongly under pressure.They shot 39 in the third set to Japan's 35 and levelled the contest at 3-3. The fourth set then went down to the final arrow, with Nakanishi shooting a 7 to finish on 35. India posted 37 to take the set and complete a 5-3 victory.The silver added to what has been a highly productive archery campaign for India in Aichi-Nagoya.Earlier on Friday, India's women's recurve team scripted a landmark triumph by defeating 10-time Olympic champions South Korea 5-3 to win the country's maiden Asian Games gold in the event.Ankita Bhakat, Kirti Sharma and 17-year-old Kumkum held their nerve in difficult windy conditions to overcome the defending champions. India had also defeated China 5-1 in the semifinal.The women's recurve gold was India's fourth archery gold of the Games, following victories in the men's compound, women's compound and mixed compound team events.
Article Summary: Kumkum Mohod and Dhiraj Bommadevara sign off with a silver medal in the mixed team recurve event. China’s Jingyi Zhu and Mengqi Li prevailed 5-3 in a closely fought gold-medal match. Indian pair had to settle for silver after fighting back from a 0-4 deficit and briefly threatening to take the contest into a deciding shoot-off.

Article Title: Gold medal secured! India’s women recurve archers defeat South Korea in final

Ankita Bhakat , Kirti Sharma and Kumkum Mohod held their nerve in windy conditions to overcome the 10-time Olympic champions in a closely fought final.The opening two sets were evenly contested, with the teams sharing the points after both produced scores of 54 and 56 respectively.South Korea then faltered in the third set.
